correctness.rationale:
The two independent arm lengths have tails p^j, with mean and second moment obtained by summing p^j and (2j-1)p^j respectively, as claimed. The expected size is strictly increasing in p; moving one step centerward changes it by p^k-p^{n-k}>0 before the center, so equality for known p identifies the reflection orbit. The full law identifies p from its all-open atom. For n=3 and 4 an independent component-interval reconstruction with exact probabilities p^(internal edges)(1-p)^(boundary edges) and factorial moments reproduced both equal-mean variance identities by polynomial remainders. The n=3 identity is strictly positive; at n=4 equal means force q

1+p+p², giving strict positivity. At n>=5 match means uniquely with q(p)

=5. Independent exact elimination using the interval moments reproduced 4p²(p-1)P(p), exact endpoint signs of the rational bracket, and the reported p, q and mean. Positivity of P' on (0,1) and the existence proof remove ambiguous and extraneous resultant roots.
residual_risks: The finding gives existence, not uniqueness, for general n>=6; the symbolic replay for small n is not the all-order proof.

value.rationale: Even with a known path and exact population moments, estimating a source orbit with unknown edge retention has a sharp loss of structural identifiability. The mechanism is the sign reversal of the variance contrast after equalizing the means, not sampling noise. The comparison to known retention and the full size law specifies exactly which observation loss is responsible in this model.
residual_risks: Does not assert indistinguishability from infection identities or full laws, applicability to correlated transmission, or finite-sample robustness.
